![**Supp. Fig. 4. _P. utriculus_ morphology.** The anterior apex of the float is marked as aaf, crest as c, gonodendra as gd, major tentacle and palpon as mt+p. A- Specimen from Queensland, Australia, with green anterior apex of the float and purple crest. The float has a sinuous appearance. Blue coloration of the major tentacle, palpons, and gastrozooids (Photo by © Richard Fuller, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), via iNaturalist Observation 318861404). B- Specimen from South Africa, two distinct purple gonodendra, clear float, and blue coloration of the float (Photo by © Johan Huisamen, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), via iNaturalist Observation 327836760). C- Specimen from Baja California, Mexico, with a blue apical apex of the float (Photo by © Bill Levine, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), via iNaturalist Observation 373121794). D- Specimen from Hainan, China, with a yellow anterior apex of the float and transparent crest (Photo by © 王琰, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), via iNaturalist Observation 303923643).](../figures/supplemental/Supp_Fig_4_P_utriculus.png)

![**Supp. Fig. 5. _P. physalis_ morphology.** The anterior apex of the float is marked as aaf, gonodendra as gd, and gastrozooids as gz. A- A South Atlantic specimen from Tobago with distinct pink coloration and reddish gastrozooids (Photo by © Trizelle, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), via iNaturalist Observation 70351531). B- South Atlantic specimen from Brazil with distinct pink coloration of the float, but the gastrozooids are blue (Photo by © nicolasteixeira, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), via iNaturalist Observation 194374632). C- North Atlantic specimen from Tenerife with a clear float and dark blue gastrozooids (Photo by © Jane Candlish, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), via iNaturalist Observation 354644470). D- Another North Atlantic specimen with clear reddish gastrozooid pigmentation (Photo by © averiemae1, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), via iNaturalist Observation 366033572).](../figures/supplemental/Supp_Fig_5_P_physalis.png)

![**Supp. Fig. 6. _Physalia_ specimens collected in Indonesia.** Based on the reported morphology [@yongstar2025physalia], they resemble specimens of the lineage "B2". A- Specimens with multiple major tentacles. B, C- The length of one of the specimens with relaxed tentacles was about 22cm. Gastrozooids with yellow distal tips visible, as well as multiple major tentacles.](../figures/supplemental/Supp_Fig_6_Indonesia_mikazuki.png)

**Supp. Fig. 7.** PLACEHOLDER — multitentacled _P. utriculus_ individuals, genetically confirmed as B1 lineage. Not yet generated (see #8).

![**Supp. Fig. 8. _P. minuta_ morphology.** The anterior apex of the float is marked as aaf, a major tentacle with an associated palpon as mt+p, and gastrozooids as gz. A- _P. minuta_ specimen from Saint Helena (YPM-IZ-115990) with two major tentacles with palpons. The anterior apex of the float is green. B- Gastrozooids with pale cream-colored distal tips of the same specimen as in panel A. C- _P. minuta_ from Tasmania, Australia. Sinuous appearance of the float, and green anterior apex of the float (Photo by © Milan Sojitra, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), via iNaturalist Observation 356379205).](../figures/supplemental/Supp_Fig_8_P_minuta.png)

![**Supp. Fig. 9. _P. megalista_ morphology.** The anterior apex of the float is marked as aaf, extension of the float is marked as eof, small extensions of the float as seof, gonodendron as gd, minor tentacles as mint, and crest as c. A- _P. megalista_ specimen from New Zealand (YPM-IZ-111515), a large specimen with one large extension of the float and a series of smaller ones spanning towards the posterior zone; gonodendron is pale compared to the rest of the blue body. B- _P. megalista_ specimen from New South Wales in a typical horned position after washing up (Photo by © Sabine Templeton, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), via iNaturalist Observation 310629814). C- _P. megalista_ specimen from South Africa with reddish coloration of minor tentacles (Photo by © spensti, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), via iNaturalist Observation 319807691). D- _P. megalista_ from New Zealand in a typical beaching posture with the anterior float projection raised; the crest has a lavender apex with green at the bases of the septae (Photo by © Paul Bell-Butler, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), via iNaturalist Observation 184621409).](../figures/supplemental/Supp_Fig_9_P_megalista.png)
